pros: Works inside VS Code, JetBrains, Visual Studio, Neovim and Xcode without switching editors
Coding agent takes a GitHub issue and opens a draft pull request
Model picker lets you switch providers per request on every plan
Enterprise admins get content exclusions, usage metrics and SAML SSO
Free tier gives 2,000 completions and 50 chat requests a month
cons: Chat is anchored to the open file unless you attach more context
Premium request allowance runs out fast under heavy agent use
Completion quality drops noticeably on niche stacks and internal frameworks
verdict_line: Pick GitHub Copilot if your team already lives on GitHub and wants AI in every existing editor with enterprise admin controls.

pros: Multi-file agent edits land as diffs you accept hunk by hunk
Repository index means chat answers cite the right files
Tab completion predicts the next edit and jumps the cursor there
Background agents run several tasks in parallel in cloud sandboxes
Rules files encode project conventions that every request follows
cons: It is a VS Code fork, so JetBrains and Neovim teams must switch
Usage-based allowance makes monthly bills variable for heavy agent use
Some VS Code extensions behave differently after import
verdict_line: Pick Cursor if you want the strongest multi-file agent workflow and can move your team onto a VS Code fork.

pros: Reviews every pull request within minutes with line-level comments
Comments include committable suggestions the author can apply in one click
Summaries and sequence diagrams explain the change before humans read it
Path-specific instructions in a YAML file fit existing team conventions
Free for public repositories on GitHub and GitLab
cons: Default settings comment generously, so large PRs get buried in nitpicks
Does not run your test suite or know business requirements
Teams that skip tuning end up ignoring the bot entirely
verdict_line: Pick CodeRabbit if you want consistent AI review comments on every pull request before a human reviewer looks.

pros: Docs site builds from MDX in your git repo on every push
OpenAPI spec generates endpoint pages and an interactive request playground
Pull requests get a preview deployment before merging
AI assistant answers reader questions and cites the pages it used
Analytics show what readers search for and which searches return nothing
cons: Opinionated layout limits unusual designs or heavy custom components
AI assistant and authenticated docs sit behind higher tiers
Pricing by editor seats and feature gating frustrates small teams
verdict_line: Pick Mintlify if your product is an API and you want polished hosted docs from markdown and an OpenAPI spec.
